coverage_notes: Visually inspected every supplied anchor on PDF pp.3,5-8,10-11; viewed p.1 title and p.2 methods. Fig.9 was additionally enlarged and actually viewed to resolve the crowded symbols. No OCR, curve tracing or automated PDF table extraction was used.
shared_qualifications: Fig.9 (PDF p.8) and its discussion (p.10) use definite pitting potentials where evident; otherwise the potential at 10 microampere/cm^2 is plotted. Individual substituted markers are not identified by the paper. Retain that conditional scientific qualification for all Fig.9 links without automatically declaring every point a proxy or excluding identities.

C9: All plotted/registered potentials are already mV vs SCE. Source sweep 60 mV/min /60 = 1 mV/s agrees with CRA. Experimental solution temperature is not supplied in the matching CSV and is not inferred.

Source method p.3 says reported results represent averages of at least three identical experiments. Graphical readings and CSV decimal strings are preserved independently; differences around marker/axis resolution are not treated as measurement precision to hundredths of a millivolt.

obs_109 source/registry disagreement: supplied registry gives Ni/NaBr/pH7 as +60 mV; enlarged visible Fig.9 open-triangle marker is approximately +20 mV, compatible with CRA 505 +18.09 mV. Identity is independently fixed by Ni, NaBr, pH7 and 1 M. Preserve the +60 mV registry and mark potential agreement discrepant.

For Fe/Ni/Mo, the source identifies elemental wire but does not report a purity assay; CSV 100.0 is treated as nominal elemental identity, not verified analytical purity. Ni80Cr20 is stated as 80% Ni:20% Cr; its percentage basis is not explicit in the source, so no at%-to-wt% conversion is invented.
